Article Title: Asian Games Medal Tally: India win 8 medals but remain outside top 10 as gold continues to elude
Article Text:
Yashvir Singh, Rohit Yadav, and Esha Singh

Eight medals, but no gold for India

Shooting and kurash add to India's tally

NEW DELHI: India produced another strong medal haul at the Asian Games 2026 on Monday, winning eight medals across athletics, shooting and kurash. However, the impressive collection did not bring any change in the overall standings, with India remaining 12th as the country continued to wait for another gold medal.India added four silver and four bronze medals during the day but could not increase its gold tally. After Day 9, India stood at 45 medals — four gold, 20 silver and 21 bronze.'The eight-medal haul included silver medals for Yashvir Singh, Murali Sreeshankar, Gulveer Singh and Esha Singh, while Rohit Yadav, Parul Chaudhary, Vithya Ramraj and Pincky Balhara won bronze.India's strongest showing came in the men's javelin, where Yashvir and Rohit produced a double podium finish in the absence of defending champion Neeraj Chopra.Yashvir recorded a personal best of 85.72m for silver, while Rohit won bronze with 84.35m. Sri Lanka's Rumesh Pathirage claimed gold with 88.55m.Sreeshankar also won silver in the men's long jump with 8.07m despite an injury forcing him to abandon his final two attempts. China's Yuhao Shi took gold with 8.17m.Gulveer added his second silver of the Games with a personal best of 3:36.72 in the men's 1500m, having earlier finished runner-up in the 10,000m.Parul Chaudhary won bronze in the women's 5000m with 15:14.61, adding to the bronze she had claimed in the 3000m steeplechase.Vithya Ramraj also took bronze in the women's 400m hurdles with a personal best of 54.75 seconds.Esha Singh secured silver in the women's 25m pistol after finishing with 38 hits, the same score as China's Xiao Jiaruixuan, who won the gold after the shoot-off.Pincky Balhara added bronze in the women's -78kg kurash category, losing 0-5 to South Korea's Sumin Mo in the semifinals.Despite the eight medals, India's gold tally remained at four, a crucial factor in the standings as countries are ranked by gold medals first.China led with 132 golds, followed by Japan with 41, South Korea with 21 and Uzbekistan with 12. India remained 12th with 45 medals, highlighting how a large haul of silver and bronze medals has yet to translate into a significant rise in the standings.
Article Summary: India added four silver and four bronze medals during the day but could not increase its gold tally. China led with 132 golds, followed by japan with 41, south korea with 21 and uzbekistan with 12. India remained 12th with 45 medals, highlighting how a large haul of silver and bronze medals has yet to translate into a significant rise in the standings.

Article Title: Jorge Jesus on Ronaldo row: 'You can’t break up a year-long friendship over a situation I can’t even understand… I don’t apologise to anyone'
Article Text:
Portugal's head coach Jorge Jesus speaks during a news conference in Copenhagen, Denmark, Wednesday, Sept. 30, 2026, ahead of their Nations League soccer match against Denmark. (Liselotte Sabroe/Ritzau Scanpix via AP)

Jorge Jesus says Ronaldo can return, but insists nothing changed his authority

Jesus backs Bruno Fernandes but refuses to apologise

Ronaldo left after being unused against Norway

Jorge Jesus has finally given his full account of the Cristiano Ronaldo controversy, and his latest comments have done little to cool the situation around Portugal. Rather than offering the apology Ronaldo was reportedly expecting, Jesus defended his decision, backed Bruno Fernandes' description of Ronaldo as the country's greatest icon and made clear that selecting the team remains entirely his responsibility.Speaking after Portugal's 2–1 Nations League victory over Norway on Sunday, Jesus addressed the dispute that began when Ronaldo left the national team camp following their previous meeting.“I don’t know what Cristiano may decide,” Jesus said. “I’ve already said what I had to say. For me, this was never an issue.”Jesus insisted that having Ronaldo as a national symbol did not mean he could not make footballing decisions involving the 41-year-old forward, particularly when he believed another choice was better for the team.“Having a player who is a symbol like him does not mean there has to be anything non-negotiable on my part as a coach. Nothing happened that called my authority into question.”Jesus also said Ronaldo remained eligible for selection in the next international window, provided he continues playing and chooses to return, while describing their relationship as one that should not be damaged permanently by what he considers a minor footballing incident.“For me, Cristiano will be eligible for selection the next time the squad is announced, provided he is playing. If he wants to, he will return to the national team. You can’t break up a year-long friendship because of a situation I can’t even understand.”Bruno Fernandes had already spoken publicly in defence of Ronaldo, insisting that his former Manchester United teammate remains the biggest figure in Portuguese football and calling for the squad to stay united.“I spoke with Cristiano and told him that he is and will always remain the GREATEST icon of our national team and our country. Our national team is united, not divided. Matters must be resolved internally and conclude well for both parties,” Fernandes said.Jesus said he completely agreed with that assessment, while revealing that he had previously spoken directly to Ronaldo about how he should view the later stages of his international career.“I completely agree with what Bruno Fernandes said. That is also my view. One of the things I told Cristiano was that he could not end his national-team career after losing at the World Cup and walking off in tears.”Jesus then returned to the decision that triggered the entire dispute and rejected the idea that he owed Ronaldo an apology for keeping him on the bench.“He was supposed to play here today, but, given everything that happened, the situation changed. Everything has been said. I am the head coach, I select whoever I want, and I don’t ask anyone who I should select or who should play.”“It was because the player had been warming up. Now, apologise for what and to whom? I don’t apologise to anyone,”he added, as per Flash Score. The dispute began when Jesus sent Ronaldo to warm up for around 30 minutes during Portugal's 2–1 Nations League victory over Norway before ultimately deciding not to use him.The decision led to an emergency meeting involving Ronaldo, Jesus and Portuguese Football Federation president Pedro Proença, but Ronaldo subsequently left the national team camp and said he would explain the reasons for his departure “in time”.Ronaldo wrote: “After the press conference of the national team and following a conversation with the president of the Portuguese Football Federation, I have decided to leave the national team training camp.”He added: “In time, I will tell all the Portuguese the truth about the reasons that motivated me to leave.”Jesus had promised to explain his side after Portugal's next match against Norway, and he has now done so, making clear that he accepts no wrongdoing over the decision while leaving the door open for Ronaldo to return.
Article Summary: Jorge jesus has given his full account of the cristiano ronaldo controversy. Portugal head coach backs bruno fernandes' description of ronaldo as the country's greatest icon. Jesus says ronaldo can return to the national team, provided he continues playing and chooses to return.

A bizarre moment during the Canada's premier T10 cricket league semi-final between Toronto Sixers and Mississauga Masters left players, commentators and fans surprised.A delivery from USA pacer Ali Khan flew over the batter and wicketkeeper before landing in the stands, but Toronto were awarded only five runs instead of six.Toronto had posted 130/4 in 10 overs, with Kieron Pollard smashing 40 from 16 balls. During the ninth over, Khan bowled a bouncer that went over Pollard and the wicketkeeper before clearing the boundary without touching the bat.The commentators initially thought it would be a wide and six. However, the umpire awarded five runs to Toronto. Under MCC laws, a six can only be given when the ball has been hit by the bat.Watch:According to Law 19.7, if a ball crosses the boundary without being struck by the bat, it is treated as a boundary four. Since the delivery was also a wide, the additional one-run wide penalty is added, making it five runs in total.Despite the unusual incident, Toronto Sixers went on to beat Mississauga Masters by nine runs and secure their place in the final. Mississauga put up a strong chase, led by Alex Lees, who smashed 39 off just 11 balls, but they could not complete the chase.In the other semi-final, Vancouver Anchors defeated Brampton Blitz by six wickets. India head coach Gautam Gambhir has opened up about his conversations with teenage batter Vaibhav Sooryavanshi and explained why the youngster had to wait for his chance despite being in good form.Sooryavanshi made history earlier this year when he became the youngest Indian to play international cricket. He made his T20I debut against England at the age of 15 years and 99 days, breaking Sachin Tendulkar’s long-standing record.He then became the youngest player to score a half-century in men’s international cricket when he reached the milestone against Zimbabwe at 15 years and 118 days.Despite his early success, Sooryavanshi did not get a game during the entire Afghanistan series or the one-off T20I against Japan ahead of the Asian Games The 15-year-old returned to the India XI in the Asian Games semifinal against Sri Lanka. He made a bigger contribution in the game, scoring 38 off 21 balls.Gambhir said he had explained to Sooryavanshi that being in good form does not always mean a player will immediately get an opportunity."It was a new experience for me as well. Yes, he was in good form, but I made him understand that sometimes, because of the players who have done well for a long time, he will have to wait for his opportunity.And there's one more thing, social media or outside noise doesn't decide the playing eleven," Gambhir said on JioStar.Gambhir said the playing XI is picked based on what the coach and captain believe is the best combination to win a match."It depends on who in that dressing room, or who the coach and captain feel can win us the match, or what is the best playing eleven, and who have done well for such a long time. Because if Vaibhav plays today, then it's going to be a tough conversation between me and whoever we leave out, whether it's Abhishek or Sanju."So, we can't suddenly ignore a combination that has created such an impact over the last one and a half or two years, and after three or four failures, drop them and play a young player who is very talented, who is also in very good form. So, sometimes you will have to wait for your opportunity because we want to create that security in that dressing room," he added.Sooryavanshi also played a part in India’s successful Asian Games title defence. He scored a quick 15 off nine balls in the final as India beat Pakistan by 19 runs to retain the gold medal.At 15 years, six months and six days, Sooryavanshi also became the youngest Indian to win an Asian Games gold medal.He surpassed shooter Saurabh Chaudhary , who was 16 years, three months and nine days old when he won the men’s 10m air pistol gold medal at the 2018 Asian Games in Jakarta.
Article Summary: Gautam gambhir explains why vaibhav sooryavanshi had to wait for his chance. The 15-year-old made history earlier this year when he became the youngest indian to play international cricket. He made his t20i debut against england at the age of 15 years and 99 days, breaking sachin tendulkar's record.

The Asian Games 2026 took place in Aichi-Nagoya, Japan, from September 19 to October 4, with athletes from 46 nations competing across various sports. India finished fourth in the medal table with 85 medals, including 21 golds, 27 silvers and 37 bronzes.India enjoyed several memorable performances, with the men’s and women’s teams winning gold medals in cricket, kabaddi and hockey. It was also the first time both Indian hockey teams won gold at the same Asian Games Among the standout individual performers was 17-year-old archer Kumkum Mohod, who became the first Indian woman to win individual recurve gold.She finished the Games with two golds and a silver. Pranavi Urs also created history by winning India’s first individual golf gold, while Neeru Dhanda became the country’s first women’s trap shooting gold medallist.At just 15, Vaibhav Sooryavanshi became India’s youngest-ever Asian Games gold medallist. The teenage batting sensation was part of the Indian men’s cricket team that defeated Pakistan by 19 runs in the final to win gold.Sooryavanshi made an aggressive start, hitting two consecutive sixes, before Saim Ayub dismissed him for 15 off nine balls. Despite his early exit, India went on to win the final and secure a memorable gold medal.Two-time Olympian Mairaj Ahmad Khan became India’s oldest medallist at the 2026 Asian Games at the age of 50. He won bronze as part of the men’s skeet shooting team alongside Anantjeet Singh Naruka and Bhavtegh Singh Gill.Khan has competed internationally for more than 20 years and is a three-time ISSF World Cup gold medallist. However, the bronze in Aichi-Nagoya was his first Asian Games medal.Overall, Japan’s 11-year-old eSports player Yuki Kurihara became the youngest gold medallist in Asian Games history after winning the Puyo Puyo Champions title. Kuwait’s 63-year-old shooter Abdullah Al-Rashidi was the oldest medallist overall, winning silver in men’s skeet.

Former India batter Hanuma Vihari has called on the team to bring experienced pacers Bhuvneshwar Kumar and Mohammed Shami back into the ODI setup. His comments came after India failed to defend 351 against the West Indies in the third ODI, losing by five wickets.Vihari believes India need more reliable bowling options instead of depending heavily on Jasprit Bumrah and Hardik Pandya for wickets, especially with the 2027 ODI World Cup less than a year away.Bhuvneshwar last played an ODI for India in 2022, with injuries affecting his career. However, the 36-year-old has remained effective in the IPL, taking 45 wickets in 30 matches across the 2025 and 2026 seasons for Royal Challengers Bengaluru.“I think they have to bring Bhuvneshwar Kumar back. In my opinion, he is still one of the best bowlers in the country. He is proving in the IPL," Vihari said on his YouTube channel.Vihari feels Bhuvneshwar's experience and control with the new ball could give India greater stability. He also believes Shami should return to strengthen the attack.“You cannot just depend on Bumrah and Hardik. You have to have backup in case of such injuries. I will say go with experience. Get Bhuvneshwar and Shami back," he said. “You will have some security with experience.When you need a breakthrough, you can go to them, and they will do the job for you. You need stability and experience will always count."Vihari described India's failure to defend a total above 350 as a major warning sign. The West Indies chased down 351 in 48.2 overs, exposing concerns about India's bowling, particularly on flat pitches.“We could not defend 350. Is this not a wake-up call? I think the team is going backwards. This is a big blow," he said.He also raised concerns over India's backup bowlers after expensive spells from Anshul Kamboj, Gurnoor Brar and Nitish Kumar Reddy.“The West Indies exposed the Indian bowling attack. They are not even part of the World Cup. Imagine top teams like Australia, South Africa, England," Vihari added.

RoI won the match by 167 runs and lifted the Irani Cup for the 33rd time, their first title since the 2023-24 season.The moment was captured in the live commentary as the commentator recalled Mukesh’s request for another over."Just before the start. He was egging him on that. I just want one over. Just one more over. Absolute Jaffa. Give me one more over and I'll give you two more wickets. Somebody hold on to Mukesh Kumar.What an over this is. Big fish. 70 odd in the first inning (Paras Dogra)," the commentator said on the live television.Mukesh Kumar and Akash Deep shared nine wickets between them as Rest of India defeated the reigning Ranji Trophy champions Jammu and Kashmir by 167 runs on the fourth day to win the Irani Cup on Sunday.Jammu and Kashmir needed 279 runs for victory but only needed to survive and draw the match to win the trophy, having taken a 41-run first-innings lead.However, Mukesh and Akash tore through the J&K batting line-up. Mukesh finished with 6/33, while Akash took three wickets as the hosts were dismissed for 111 and RoI won the match by 167 runs.
Article Summary: Mukesh kumar and akash deep shared nine wickets between them as rest of india defeated the reigning ranji trophy champions jammu and kashmir by 167 runs on the fourth day to win the irani cup. Article Title: NBA injury update: Spurs coach drops latest status on $31 million forward ahead of NBA season opener
Article Text:

How the Spurs lineup could look without him

Tobias Harris' injury update from San Antonio came with no timetable attached. Coach Mitch Johnson told reporters Sunday that the Spurs will let a left calf strain heal at its own pace, even with the season opener against the Oklahoma City Thunder on Oct. 20 getting close.San Antonio signed Harris this offseason to share the frontcourt with Victor Wembanyama, and his first camp has been interrupted by a strain with no firm return date. The $31 million forward sat out the weekend scrimmage and will be checked again once the preseason wraps up.Tobias Harris, 34, strained a left calf muscle in training camp, and the Spurs made the news public Sunday. The team lists Harris as questionable for the Oct. 20 opener and says a fresh evaluation will come after the preseason. Roughly two weeks separate the announcement from opening night.The Spurs announced the strain, Tom Orsborn of the San Antonio Express-News reported that Harris would not suit up for the scrimmage, and Johnson addressed it afterward at Frost Bank Center, "We won't rush him at all."The coach added that the staff sees no cause for alarm at this level of seriousness, though he stopped short of rating the strain.Asked about the opener, Johnson said Harris' availability is very much in doubt and the team will not push him toward that game. San Antonio has not given a return date or a number of weeks, so the next real update comes when Harris is reevaluated after the preseason, which opens Oct. 8 at home against the Atlanta Hawks and runs five games.The 6-foot-8 forward is not an easy piece to replace. Harris spent the past two seasons in Detroit, and last year the Pistons won 60 games and finished first in the East while Harris averaged 13.3 points, 5.1 rebounds and 2.5 assists over 63 appearances. Harris also shot 46.9% from the field and 36.8% from three in 27.7 minutes a night.San Antonio saw a big offseason pickup in those numbers. The idea was to add veteran presence and versatility to a team coming off a historic run to the 2026 NBA Finals. Harris was projected as the main frontcourt partner for Wembanyama, and the two-year, $31 million contract makes this more than a depth issue. Harris lists at small forward and power forward, so the injury touches more than one spot in the rotation.Without Harris, the Spurs will likely turn to the group that carried them last year, including Wembanyama, De'Aaron Fox, Stephon Castle, Devin Vassell and Julian Champagnie, with Dylan Harper coming off the bench. Carter Bryant, Harrison Barnes and Keldon Johnson give the staff extra options while Harris heals.

Article Title: The road to LA 2028: How Sjoerd Marijne and his team rebuilt India's women's hockey side
Article Text:
Image credit: Hockey India

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

At the Gifu Prefectural Green Stadium, tears flowed freely on the pitch. More than 5,500km away, in India, women’s hockey’s loyal legion, small in numbers but deep in investment, rejoiced.They had watched a team in which skill was matched by fitness, individual brilliance was backed by teamwork and, finally, belief had returned.The gold medal, won after 44 years, was defining. But the direct ticket to the Los Angeles Olympics was unprecedented.Interest in women’s hockey had gathered pace after India’s fourth-place finish at the Tokyo Olympics. Missing out on Paris, however, dented the hopes and aspirations that had begun to build.Then came the well-documented rifts, allegations, a dip in form and a spate of injuries. The shadow over Los Angeles grew darker.Enter Sjoerd Marijne and his support staff. They did not have a magic wand to make the demons disappear. What they brought was a systematic approach to rebuilding the physical and psychological framework of the team.The Dutchman was quick to point out that rebuilding a team is never the work of one person.“There’s a great connection among the staff and the players. I’m doing the interviews, but it’s an achievement from the whole staff. I’m really happy with all the quality I have around me,” he said.But there was another requirement, ensuring the players were fit enough to play as one.That was where Wayne Lombard, the team’s head of athletic performance, came in. He had a broad idea of the physical state of the squad when he arrived.The support staff hit the reset button. Rodet Yila and Caira Yila were brought in as scientific advisers, while the immediate priority was not fitness for fitness’ sake, but getting the players healthy.“Regardless of what the fitness levels were, the priority was to address the injury concerns,” Lombard said.That required more than exercises and numbers. The players had to believe in the process.“We had to sit down with the players and earn their buy-in. Helping them understand that the physical side of the game is every bit as important as the technical and tactical side,” Lombard said.He introduced the 30-15 intermittent fitness test to establish the players’ maximum aerobic speed. The test required them to run for 30 seconds, rest for 15 and progress across a 40m grid, with the speed increasing by 0.5kmph at every stage.Muscle by muscle, the players rebuilt their strength. With it came confidence.As the year progressed, India began to look increasingly like a team t rather than a collection of talented individuals.Poetic justice or coincidence, Japan had stood in India’s way in the qualifiers for the Paris Olympics. In Japan, a little over two years later, India cleared the hurdle to Los Angeles.
Article Summary: The gold medal, won after 44 years, was defining. But the direct ticket to the los angeles olympics was unprecedented. Sjoerd marijne and his support staff did not have a magic wand to make the demons disappear. What they brought was a systematic approach to rebuilding the physical and psychological framework of the team.

India’s medal-winning campaign at the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games 2026 has reached 80 medals, with the contingent winning 18 gold, 26 silver and 36 bronze medals. India are currently fifth in the overall medal standings.India’s medal tally received a major boost over the last two days, with the contingent adding gold medals across boxing, wrestling, archery, hockey and golf. Lovlina Borgohain, Parveen Hooda, Ankush Panghal, Sujeet Kalkal, the Indian women’s hockey team, Kumkum Mohod and Pranavi Urs have all contributed gold medals to India’s latest surge.Kumkum also won silver alongside Dhiraj Bommadevara in the mixed recurve team event, while India’s women’s golf team of Pranavi Urs, Aditi Ashok and Diksha Dagar secured silver.On October 3, Kumkum Mohod added another gold by winning the women’s individual recurve event. The 17-year-old defeated South Korea’s Oh Yejin 6-5 in a shoot-off to become the first Indian woman to win an individual recurve medal at the Asian Games. Her victory also secured an Olympic quota place for India for the 2028 Los Angeles Games.Pranavi Urs also scripted history by becoming the first Indian woman to win individual golf gold at the Asian Games, while helping India claim silver in the women’s team event alongside Aditi Ashok and Diksha Dagar.India’s women’s cricket team won the country’s first gold medal of the Games after defeating Sri Lanka in the final. Suruchi Singh and Kamaljeet then added India’s second gold by winning the 10m air pistol mixed team event.India subsequently won both the men’s and women’s kabaddi titles, while Neeru Dhanda secured gold in the women’s trap event. She later teamed up with Kynan Chenai to win the mixed trap team gold.In athletics, Kiran Pahal, Poovamma Machettira, Prachi Choudhary and Vithya Ramraj won gold in the women’s 4x400m relay. India also dominated the compound archery events, winning gold in the men’s team, women’s team and mixed team events.On October 2, Lovlina Borgohain defeated China’s Bao Ziyi 5-0 in the women’s 75kg final to win gold. The victory came on her birthday and made Lovlina only the second Indian woman boxer after Mary Kom to win an Asian Games gold.The women’s recurve team of Ankita Bhakat, Kirti Sharma and Kumkum Mohod then created history by defeating South Korea 5-3 to win India’s first-ever Asian Games gold in the event.India then added three more gold medals in boxing and wrestling, with Parveen Hooda winning the women’s 65kg title, Ankush Panghal taking gold in the men’s 80kg category and Sujeet Kalkal winning the men’s freestyle 65kg event.The Indian women’s hockey team ended a 44-year wait for Asian Games gold by defeating China 1-0 in the final, with the victory also securing a direct qualification spot for the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics.On October 3, Kumkum completed a memorable Asian Games campaign by winning individual recurve gold. After being pushed to a shoot-off by Oh Yejin, the 17-year-old held her nerve to shoot a 10 and beat the South Korean 8, securing India’s first individual women’s recurve gold at the Asian Games.Pranavi Urs added another historic gold in golf. The 23-year-old became the first Indian woman to win an individual golf gold medal at the Asian Games. She also helped India win silver in the women’s team event.India’s silver medal haul has come across shooting, athletics, weightlifting, wushu, squash, wrestling, sailing, archery and golf.The shooting contingent has been one of India’s biggest contributors, with medals across air rifle, 50m rifle 3 positions, 25m pistol and trap events.Mirabai Chanu ended her long wait for an Asian Games medal by taking silver in the women’s 49kg weightlifting event, while Roshibina Devi won silver in women’s 60kg sanda. Gulveer Singh also enjoyed a strong Games, winning silver in the men’s 10,000m and 1500m events.In squash, Anahat Singh and Abhay Singh won silver in the women’s and men’s singles events respectively. Article Title: 'Coach and captain want to give longer rope to certain players': KL Rahul reveals India's 2027 World Cup plans
Article Text:
KL Rahul (Image credit: BCCI)

‘Trying to play with softer, older balls’

India want to push towards 370-380

Rahul wanted more time in the middle

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: India batter KL Rahul says he is working on improving his game against the old ball so that he can help the team score more runs in the middle overs.Rahul spoke to JioStar after scoring 129 off 87 balls in the third ODI against West Indies. India posted 351, but the total was not enough as the visitors chased it down in 48.2 overs.India had already won the series after taking the first two games.Rahul said batting in the final 10 overs becomes difficult when the ball gets old and starts to reverse swing."It's not been easy to get 80-90 in the last 10 overs. The ball's been getting reverse swing, and even in this game, once the ball got old and soft, and started to reverse swing, as a batter you don't feel confident enough to take on the long-on and deep mid-wicket fielder if it's a big boundary on that side," he said.Rahul said he is now working on finding ways to attack the older ball, especially because he naturally prefers facing a harder ball."...I like the hard ball coming onto me, I can use the pace. So that's something I've been working on, trying to play with softer, older balls and being able to hit sixes with that."I constantly try to get better within my own game, understand my role, understand what a number five and number six batter has to do to consistently put up performances for the team," he added.Rahul also spoke about India’s preparations for the ODI World Cup in South Africa next year.With teams regularly chasing big totals, Rahul said 340 or 350 is no longer always a safe score. He believes India’s middle order must find ways to score faster and push the team towards 370 or 380.West Indies chased 352 in 48.2 overs in the third ODI. India had also chased a record 406 in the second ODI in Guwahati, completing the chase in just 43.2 overs."We don't want to go too far away from the plan but also experiment a little bit as a batting unit. The goal so far has been about can we score 330-340 while batting first, but we're seeing that 340s and 350s get chased down very easily in one-day cricket," he said."So how can batters, once set, keep pressing on and get 370s and 380s, or push for 400 on a given day. The minute we as middle-order batters go in, the aim is to ensure that we do not take too much time to get going and start rotating the strike and keep hitting a boundary every six or seven balls."The coach and captain have been very clear on the personnel they want to bring in. They want to give a longer rope to certain players who we feel might be important for the World Cup," he explained.Rahul has been batting at No. 5 or No. 6 for some time. He said his 129 against West Indies was important because it allowed him to spend a long time at the crease and test the changes he has been making to his batting."I wanted to spend more time with the bat out there in the middle and the last time I really got to bat for a long duration in ODI cricket, in the middle-order was in early January this year against New Zealand, and since then I haven't really got a lot of time to play a long innings."And next year is a big one, with the World Cup starting in October, so it's important for me to get valuable batting time because off the field I'm trying a few things and I want to test that in the game."And only then will you know whether the work that you're putting behind the scenes is working or not, or what I need to do differently. So yeah, it was important for me to get some batting time," he said.
Article Summary: Rahul scored 129 off 87 balls in the third odi against west indies. India posted 351, but the total was not enough as the visitors chased it down in 48.2 overs. Rahul said batting in the final 10 overs becomes difficult when the ball gets old and starts to reverse swing.

Article Title: An $80,000 statue of an 1886 Kentucky Derby winner was stolen in California; thieves sawed through its legs and left one hoof behind
Article Text:
The 1886 Kentucky Derby winner behind the statue

The $80,000 statue became a Sacramento landmark

Thieves sawed through the bronze horse's legs

Only one hoof was left behind

Police are searching for the missing statue

An $80,000 life-size bronze statue of Ben Ali, the horse that won the 1886 Kentucky Derby, has been stolen from a road median in Sacramento, California. The nearly 7-foot statue had stood on Del Paso Boulevard for almost two decades and commemorated the horse’s connection to the city’s historic Rancho Del Paso. When the theft was discovered, only a single bronze hoof remained attached to the concrete base. Sacramento police are investigating the disappearance and have asked the public for information about the statue or those responsible. The theft has removed a distinctive landmark from North Sacramento and left behind an unusual mystery over how a large bronze horse was taken from a public location.Ben Ali won the 12th Kentucky Derby at Churchill Downs in 1886 and became the first horse with a California connection to win the race. He was associated with Rancho Del Paso, a major horse-breeding operation in the Sacramento area. The ranch was established by James Ben Ali Haggin and became one of the most prominent thoroughbred breeding operations in the United States during the late 19th century. Ben Ali’s Derby victory became part of the region’s racing history and helped preserve the connection between the horse and Sacramento. More than a century later, that history was commemorated with a bronze statue on Del Paso Boulevard.The sculpture was created to honour Ben Ali and recognise his association with the historic Rancho Del Paso.The life-size bronze statue was installed on Del Paso Boulevard in 2007 and formally dedicated in 2008. It stood near the Sacramento Youth Center in the 1900 block of Del Paso Boulevard at Winnipeg Street. The sculpture was positioned on a concrete base in the road median and became a familiar feature of the North Sacramento neighbourhood. The statue was valued at approximately $80,000 and represented more than an artwork because it commemorated a specific chapter in the city's history. For nearly two decades, residents and people travelling through the area could see the bronze horse standing at the site connected to Ben Ali’s legacy. Its disappearance has now left an empty space where the historic monument once stood.The theft was discovered after the statue was removed from its concrete mounting. Reports said the thieves sawed through the bronze legs to take the horse, leaving one hoof behind on the base. The remaining hoof and severed section of the sculpture provided a visible indication of how the monument had been removed. Taking a nearly 7-foot bronze statue would have required considerable effort and some means of transporting the heavy sculpture away from the site. Despite the unusual nature of the theft, investigators have not publicly established a motive. It is also unclear whether the thieves intended to sell the bronze for scrap, resell the artwork or had another reason for targeting the monument. Police are continuing to investigate the circumstances surrounding the disappearance.The theft has drawn attention because of the unusual scene left at the former location. Instead of finding the complete statue, people were left with the concrete base and a single bronze hoof. Images of the site show the severed section where the horse had previously stood, highlighting the scale of the theft. Community members have expressed disappointment over the loss because the statue was a visible reminder of North Sacramento’s connection to thoroughbred racing. The monument also carried historical significance because of Ben Ali’s connection to Rancho Del Paso and his Kentucky Derby victory. Replacing the sculpture would be expensive, with reports putting its value at around $80,000. The city does not have immediate funds set aside to replace it.Sacramento police are investigating the theft and have asked anyone who may have information to contact authorities. Investigators are working to determine who removed the statue and where it may have been taken. The Del Paso Boulevard Business Association has also drawn attention to the disappearance as community members hope the sculpture can be recovered. The case remains open and there is no confirmed motive for the theft. Until the statue is found, the single bronze hoof is the only remaining piece visible at its former location. What began as a monument to an 1886 Kentucky Derby winner has therefore become the centre of an unusual modern-day theft investigation in Sacramento.
Article Summary: Ben ali won the 12th kentucky derby at churchill downs in 1886. He was associated with rancho del paso, a major horse-breeding operation in the sacramento area. A bronze statue of ben ali was installed on del paso boulevard in 2007 and formally dedicated in 2008.

Article Title: Lionel Messi's foundation helped fund a €37 million childhood cancer centre in Barcelona; when it opened in 2022, the hospital gained capacity to see up to 400 new cancer cases a year
Article Text:
In 2012, the Leo Messi Foundation contributed funding to the Sports for Peace programme in Colombia, which used sport to support young people living in communities affected by violence.

From an idea to a landmark centre

A wider commitment to children

Taking the mission beyond Barcelona

A different kind of Barcelona legacy

For all the stadiums, trophies and record books associated with Lionel Messi, some of the most lasting chapters of his Barcelona story were written far from the football pitch. One of them took shape through a project aimed at children facing cancer. The Leo Messi Foundation was among the organizations that helped bring the SJD Pediatric Cancer Center Barcelona to life, creating a specialist facility where treatment, research and family support could exist under one roof, states an online report on Bein Sports. Scroll down to read the details.According to Bein Sports, the project was promoted by Hospital Sant Joan de Déu, with the Leo Messi Foundation involved before construction even began. Its early contribution helped finance the centre's architectural development and supported the launch of the fundraising campaign. The foundation later became one of the project's 10 founding donors. In October 2018, with €2.6 million still needed to reach the €30 million fundraising target required to secure construction, the Leo Messi Foundation and Stavros Niarchos Foundation stepped in to jointly provide the remaining amount the report adds.The centre eventually opened its doors in 2022, creating additional capacity to treat childhood cancer patients and allowing the hospital to attend to as many as 400 new cancer cases each year, claims the online report.The Barcelona cancer centre fits into a charitable effort that Messi has built over many years. His foundation, established in 2007, has focused largely on projects benefiting children and teenagers living in vulnerable circumstances.His work with UNICEF has been another important part of that commitment. Messi became a UNICEF Goodwill Ambassador in 2010 and has since supported initiatives involving education, health and child protection.In 2012, the Leo Messi Foundation contributed funding to the Sports for Peace programme in Colombia, which used sport to support young people living in communities affected by violence. Five years later, the foundation helped finance 20 prefabricated classrooms in Syria, enabling more than 1,600 children affected by conflict to return to school, the report also states.Messi's move to Inter Miami added another chapter to that work. In 2025, the Inter Miami CF Foundation and UNICEF began a three-year partnership supporting educational programmes for children in Argentina, El Salvador, Haiti, Honduras and Mexico. Messi also contributed to the partnership through an unusual fundraising project. He selected his header against Manchester United in the 2009 Champions League final as his favourite career goal and worked with artist Refik Anadol to transform it into a digital artwork, A Goal in Life. Christie's later auctioned the piece for $1.87 million, with proceeds benefiting several nonprofit organizations, including initiatives connected to the Inter Miami-UNICEF partnership.Messi's life away from football has also expanded into hospitality, real estate, gastronomy and other business ventures. Yet the SJD Pediatric Cancer Center represents a different dimension of that legacy. It was not a one-off gesture but a project that developed over years, from architectural planning and fundraising to the eventual opening of a dedicated childhood cancer centre. Long after Messi's playing days in Barcelona ended, the project left something tangible behind, a place built around children, families and the difficult fight against cancer.
Article Summary: Lionel messi's foundation helped bring the sjd pediatric cancer center barcelona to life. The project was promoted by hospital sant joan de déu, with the leo messi foundation involved before construction even began. Its early contribution helped finance the centre's architectural development and supported the launch of the fundraising campaign.

Article Title: IND vs WI: Why India and West Indies were fined after 3rd ODI
Article Text:
India vs West Indies 3rd ODI (ANI Photo/Rahul Singh)

West Indies end ODI series on a high

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

India and the West Indies have been fined for maintaining slow over-rates during the third and final ODI of their three-match series in New Chandigarh on Saturday.India were four overs behind the required rate after time allowances were taken into account, while the West Indies were two overs short. As a result, India were fined 20 per cent of their match fee, while the West Indies received a 10 per cent fine."In accordance with Article 2.22 of the ICC Code of Conduct for Players and Player Support Personnel, which relates to minimum over-rate offences, players are fined five per cent of their match fee for every over their side fails to bowl in the allotted time," the ICC said in a statement.Both captains accepted the charges and the proposed sanctions, meaning there was no need for a formal hearing.The penalties were imposed by Prakash Bhatt of the ICC International Panel of Match Referees.On-field umpires Jayaraman Madanagopal and Sam Nogajski, third umpire Sharfuddoula Ibne Shahid and fourth umpire Virender Sharma had levelled the charges.The West Indies had already lost the three-match series 2-0 before the final ODI, but they finished the series with a memorable win.Led by an unbeaten 162 from captain Shai Hope, the visitors successfully chased down 352, recording their highest successful run chase in ODI cricket.Their previous best was 331/5 against Ireland in 2019.Hope also created history with his innings. He became the first wicketkeeper-captain to score more than 150 runs in an ODI innings.His knock was also the highest score by a West Indies men's batter in a successful ODI chase, surpassing Brian Lara's 153 against Pakistan in Sharjah in 1993.With the ODI series now over, India and the West Indies will shift their focus to the five-match T20I series, which begins on Tuesday.
Article Summary: India and west indies fined for slow over-rates in third odi. India were four overs behind the required rate after time allowances. West indies were two overs short. India fined 20 per cent of their match fee, while the west indies received a 10 per cent fine.

Article Title: Shattering records and cultivating future stars
Article Text:
Mayura Shanbaug

Ashish Kumar Srivastava - MD and CEO of PNB MetLife

Sameer Bansal - Chief Distribution Officer of PNB MetLife

Chirag Shetty - Asian Games Gold Medalist & JBC 2023 mentor

Satwiksairaj Rankireddy - Asian Games Gold Medalist & JBC 2023 mentor

Disclaimer: Content Produced by PNB Metlife

The 7th PNB MetLife Junior Badminton Championship shattered records with over 8,200 young talent nationwide, earning global recognition and fostering a culture of resilience and determination in aspiring badminton starsIn a spectacular display of badminton prowess and youthful enthusiasm, the 7th edition of the PNB MetLife Junior Badminton Championship (JBC) etched its name in the annals of sporting history. Celebrating a staggering participation of 8257 young champions from across India, the championship not only broke its own record set in 2022 but also clinched the title of the ‘Most kids participating in a Badminton Championship in multiple cities’ as recognised by the World Record Certification Agency (WRCA).The grand finale unfolded at the Indira Gandhi Indoor Stadium in New Delhi, where the air was thick with competition, camaraderie, and the unmistakable passion for badminton. The event, graced by chief guests Chirag Shetty and Satwik Rankireddy, Asian Games Gold Medalists and JBC 2023 mentors, was a true celebration of the sport’s rising stars.The 10-city extravaganza, spanning the length and breadth of the country, showcased the unwavering commitment of PNB MetLife in nurturing young talents in the badminton arena. With participants exceeding 8200, it’s evident that the PNB MetLife JBC has become a beacon for aspiring shuttlers, highlighting the deep-seated passion for badminton among the diverse and talented youth of India.Beyond the glitz and glamour of the record-breaking numbers, the championship holds a special place in the hearts of those at the helm. Ashish Kumar Srivastava, MD and CEO of PNB MetLife, expressed pride in not just surpassing their own world record but also in contributing to India’s glory on the international badminton stage. The championship, he emphasized, is not merely a competition but a significant milestone in creating a pan-India badminton ecosystem.This edition of the JBC saw a strategic partnership with world champions Chirag Shetty and Satwiksairaj Rankireddy, who served as mentors for the young talents. Sameer Bansal, Chief Distribution Officer of PNB MetLife, acknowledged the pivotal role played by these champions in inspiring the next generation of badminton stars. The focus, according to Bansal, is on unleashing the latent potential of young shuttlers and preparing them for global excellence.The Delhi chapter of the championship witnessed some nail-biting action with over 1000 participants competing fiercely across various categories. From Ananya Talyan’s stellar performance in Girls Singles Under 9 to Divyansh Rawat’s triumph in Boys Singles Under 17, the young talents left no shuttle unturned in their quest for victory.The results from the Delhi leg not only showcased the raw talent but also highlighted the championship’s commitment to breaking barriers. The PNB MetLife Junior Badminton Championship is not just about records; it’s about fostering a culture of healthy living, determination, and resilience among the future champions of the sport.In the words of Satwiksairaj Rankireddy, the championship serves as an invaluable platform.---------------------------------------------------------------As we celebrate the successful culmination of the 7th edition of PNB MetLife Junior Badminton Championship , we take pride in surpassing our own world record for highest participation and for being recognized by World Record Certification Agency. Beyond the records, JBC represents a significant milestone in our mission to lay the groundwork for India’ s glory and success on the international badminton stage by creating a pan-India badminton ecosystem that nurtures champions at the grassroots levelThis year has been especially remarkable for PNB MetLife JBC as we joined hands with world champions Chirag Shetty and Satwiksairaj Rankireddy as JBC Mentors for the young talents associated with this tournament. They have played a pivotal role in inspiring young shuttlers to dream big and elevate their game and skills. We are eager for the next edition to unfold in our journey of unveiling the latent badminton potential across our nation and preparing them for global excellenceIt’s inspiring to witness the boundless talent and enthusiasm within our young athletes. My journey as JBC mentor has been incredibly fulfilling, as I got the opportunity to guide these budding champions and witness the journey of these young badminton stars. This championship is more than a competition; it is a platform that nurtures dreams, ignites aspirations, and, I believe, it is laying the foundation for future gold medalists in the makingTournaments like these serve as an invaluable platform for nurturing and harnessing the potential of our country’s young badminton stars. Witnessing the enthusiasm, passion, and skill displayed by these emerging shuttlers reinforces the belief that our country has an immense reservoir of talent. My association as a JBC mentor has been a source of immense pride, particularly given the role that the championship is playing in creating an incredible platform that is serving as a powerful catalyst, empowering young players and bolstering their confidence to become future champions
Article Summary: The 7th pnb metlife junior badminton championship shattered records with over 8,200 young talent nationwide. The grand finale unfolded at the indira gandhi indoor stadium in new delhi, where the air was thick with competition, camaraderie, and the unmistakable passion for badminton.
